messages:
Nora (PMM): quick flag - draft launch post mentions "strong organic lift" from yesterday afternoon but the KPI slide shows a strange bump in 'social -> demo' conversions. pls confirm before we publish.
Hector (Analytics): looking. initial quick-check: some influencer links used shortlink service that strips utm_ prefix, landing with param 'src' instead of 'utm_source'. our pipeline doesn't map that, so counts are split.
Jin (Social): ah yes the influencer sent links via bit.ly and one partner used ?src=ig_story. my bad, should've enforced the canonical utm tag.
Priya (Growth): request: can we show both 'reported' and 'canonicalized' numbers in the KPI slide? canonicalize by mapping `src`->`utm_source` and normalizing campaign keys.
Hector (Analytics): small SQL patch: `SELECT COALESCE(params->>'utm_medium', params->>'src') as medium_key, COUNT(*) as hits FROM web_events ...` I'll push a staging panel with side-by-side bars.
OpsBot: dashboard-staging deploy queued at 1760000040 by Hector.
Nora (PMM): hold the launch post language referencing organic hotspot. we'll update once Hector drops the normalized chart.
Hector (Analytics): deployed at 1760000060. normalized uplift is +9% (was +28% raw). panels: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/panels/2001/social-normalize.png
Jin (Social): I'll resend influencer brief to require utm_ keys and update the shortlink templates.
Priya (Growth): please add a one-line footnote to the launch: "Normalized metrics reconcile different shortlink parameter conventions; raw counts available for audit."
Nora (PMM): thanks all. tasks: 1) Hector - attach final images 2) Jin - update influencer templates 3) Priya - add footnote. I'll approve the post once images are in. closing thread after PR goes live. :white_check_mark:
